newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour denies planning shake-up at BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour denies planning shake-up at BBC.

text.p: The Labour Party on Wednesday denied it planned a major shake-up at the British Broadcasting Corporation if it comes to power at the upcoming election.

"There are no plans in existence to cause upheaval at the BBC," the opposition party's National Heritage spokesman Jack Cunningham said in a statement issued in response to a story in the Guardian newspaper.

The Guardian suggested that Labour would strip the BBC governors of most of their powers and create a new body, the Office of Communications, by merging the Independent Television Commission (ITC) with Oftel, the telecommunications industry regulator.
But Cunningham said the establishment of an Ofcom to regulate broadcasting and telephony had been proposed in a Labour policy document in 1995, which had also suggested restructuring the ITC.

"The Guardian story about Labour and the BBC is a huge over-reaction to ideas and thoughts which have been around for some time. Their story has no foundations," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
